title: Embedding calibration & drift sentinel: nightly eval + rerank latency probes
creator: Ariana Patel
description:
Objective: Build a production-ready evaluation harness that runs nightly to validate embedding accuracy and reranking fidelity, detect distribution drift, and capture latency/backpressure signals for the reranking endpoint. The harness will combine curated anchor sets (small high-quality reference queries + human-labeled relevance tiers), synthetic perturbations, and production-sampled traffic probes to provide both offline quality metrics and operational alerts.

Why: We have observed intermittent regressions after model swaps and quantization profile changes; current alerts are noisy and slow. A focused nightly sentinel will surface systematic quality shifts, and adding lightweight rerank latency probes will correlate quality changes with SLO violations.

Scope:
- Curate a compact "anchor" reference corpus (2k queries across domains, with graded relevance labels) stored in s3://redwood-embed-gold/anchor-v1/
- Nightly batch job that computes: recall@1/5/10, MRR, NDCG@10, mean cosine drift, calibration_score (distance -> rerank score monotonicity), and a lightweight rerank latency microbenchmark (p95/p99 token latency and end-to-end rerank latency).
- Drift detectors: population KS test on cosine similarity distributions, centroid shift cosine, and online change point detection on MRR using EWMA; configurable thresholds per-customer and global baselines.
- Alerting: If drift or quality regression exceeds thresholds, create a ticket, send Slack/SRE paged runbook link, and attach a snapshot of top failing queries and histogram diffs.
- Telemetry: Emit deltas into Grafana dashboard and Record in BigQuery daily table for longitudinal analysis.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Nightly job runs successfully for last 7 consecutive nights on staging and sends artifacts to s3 and BigQuery.
2) Calculated metrics (recall@k, MRR, NDCG) have stable baselines and documented test harness reproducibility (seeded).
3) Drift detectors fire with <5% false positive rate on synthetic non-drift runs and detect injected drift scenarios in internal tests.
4) Rerank latency microbenchmark correlates with observed production SLO violations in at least two historical incidents.
5) Runbook and automated ticket creation implemented; on-drift action triggers an ENG triage workflow.

Implementation plan:
- Week 1: Anchor set curation (PM + Research + Data team) and schema (label tiers, canonical query canonicalization).
- Week 2: Batch evaluation job (Spark/Beam) to compute offline metrics + synthetic perturbations generator.
- Week 3: Lightweight rerank probe harness (go microclient) and integration into nightly flow.
- Week 4: Drift detectors, thresholds, dashboards, and alerting hooks.
- Week 5: Runbook, automation for ticketing, and staging validation.

Artifacts:
- Confluence design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/Embed+Calibration+Sentinel (design + thresholds)
- Proto PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1482
- Dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/embeds/embedding-quality-sentinel
- Anchor S3: s3://redwood-embed-gold/anchor-v1/
updates: 2025-02-15 — Triage: initial scope and owner assigned. Ariana curated initial anchor set candidates (1200 queries across docs, chat, queries).

2025-02-17 — Decision: use seeded synthetic perturbations (token dropout, paraphrase, template swap) to create drift tests; flagged need for human relabeling of 300 ambiguous queries — assigned to DataOps.
2025-02-19 — Design review: team (Eng, Research, PM) agreed on metrics: recall@1/5/10, MRR, NDCG@10, calibration monotonicity. Action: Diego to prototype Beam job for nightly metrics.
2025-02-21 — PR opened: infra/pull/1482 contains batch job scaffolding and S3 integration. Requesting review from infra and observability.
2025-02-23 — Blocker: Observability team noted missing BigQuery dataset permissions for service account; ticket created ENG-48590 to provision. Working with SRE.

2025-02-25 — Prototype results: staging run on anchor-v1 shows baseline MRR=0.62, recall@1=0.48. Synthetic drift injection (add gaussian noise to embeddings) reduced recall@1 by 0.12 and fired KS alpha=0.01. Need to tune alert thresholds to reduce noise from small runtime fluctuations.
2025-02-28 — Infra PR merged for rerank probe client (infra/pull/1497). Next: wire probe to nightly pipeline and add dashboard panels for p95/p99 latencies. Preparing runbook for triage flow.
notes: Trade-offs: small anchor sets are manageable and fast to run nightly but may miss low-frequency regressions; plan to add periodic full-corpus runs weekly.
Calibration approach: we will compute monotonicity score instead of trying to map distance to absolute probabilities to avoid brittleness across model families.
Alerting policy: start with conservative thresholds and collect 14 days of signal before escalating to paging for P1 customers.
